concurrent_checks: tail vs footer 0x60 hash comparison (Section 13.3 step 1): the footer still carries the primary's hash, so on the Recoverer's footer-first route the tail is simply invalid against the locator
integrity_repair: R-SC-HASHED applied to the tail copy (canonical_metadata_hash 0x98, header_crc64 0xC0, block0_crc64 B-8)

mutation.effect: each copy on its own satisfies Sections 9.2-9.5 (the tail's hash is recomputed over its own entries); the copies differ in index content and in canonical_metadata_hash
mutation.field: data_shard_crc64 of data-CRC entry 0 (ordinal 0) in the tail copy

pin_note: Pinned for the per-sidecar validation outcome (a Section 9 violation, SidecarParse). The Recoverer's tape-level consequence is not decided; see NOTES.md.
quotes: The tail copy MUST carry metadata and index content identical to the primary; only `copy_kind` and the recomputed CRCs differ. When both copies parse, a Reader MUST verify that they agree and reject divergence.
tape_level: Unpinned. Verifier: reports the divergence (SidecarParse). Recoverer: step 1 verifies both copies against the footer; only the primary matches the footer's hash, so the primary is 'valid' and used, and epoch 0 appears usable; but Section 9.1 also says to 'reject divergence' when both copies parse, which could instead make the epoch's metadata unusable (SidecarMetadataUnavailable{0}). The text does not say which copy, if any, survives a divergence.
target: primary/tail agreement check (Section 9.1), as run by a Verifier reading both copies
why_defined: Section 9.1 writes the contract down: the tail copy MUST be identical to the primary except copy_kind and CRCs, and when both copies parse a Reader MUST verify agreement and reject divergence.
